# Establishment log — bardo-thodol-011 (pp. 98–107), 2026-11-22

Text **ga**, the third part. It covers day twelve (Karma Heruka) and the start of the wrathful goddesses: the eight Gaurīs, the eight Phra men, the four gatekeepers, the introduction to the twenty-eight Īśvarīs, and the eastern six.
There is no transcription of this print for ga. So three readers (all on the strongest model; no Sonnet role ran) read the images line by line from scratch, with the other recension (readings/witness_ga.txt) open only as a guide:
- Reader A read 98.3 (rest)–101.
- Reader B read 102–104.
- Reader C read 105–107, and p. 108 only to see where the sentence ends.

Each reader checked the line where their pages meet the next reader's, and both seams are clean. A's reading of 98.3–5 also agrees letter for letter with what C wrote for part 010. The full tables are in readings/read_A-log.md, read_B-log.md and read_C-log.md. The editor (this firing) looked at 102.5 again at ×4 on a straightened copy and kept B's reading with its marks.

## Layout
- Every page has five lines.
- pp. 99, 101, 103, 105 and 107 are leaf fronts and open with the ornament, written ༄༅༔ ༔.
- Every image from n99 to n109 is skewed by 1.4–2.0°, so all of them were read from straightened copies.
- **Start.** The part starts on 98.3 with ཡང་དེ་ལྟར, after 010's …སངས་རྒྱས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ༔.
- **End.** The part ends at the end of 107.2 with …ཤར་གྱི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་མ་དྲུག་…འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ༔ དེ་ལ་མ་འཇིགས་ཤིག༔, which closes the eastern six Īśvarīs.
  - **Part 012 begins at 107.3** with ཀྱཻ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ལྷོ་ནས… (the southern six).
  - Reader C's transcription of 107.3–5 is in readings/read_C.txt and can be used as a draft reading for 012. It includes a gap at 107.3: དགའ་བ་སེར་མོ་[…]་མགོ, an animal head of two syllables ending in ད (the other recension's ཕག does not fit the traces). There is also a [?] at 107.5 སྤྲའི.

## Doubtful readings marked [?] (13 marks)
- 100.3 རྩལ.
- 101.1 རིག་པ (other recension རགས་པ "coarse"; the image shows a vowel sign over ར and no ས). The sense wants རགས་པ, so this may be a misprint; it is kept, note only.
- 101.2 བླ in སྔར་གོང་དུ་བླ་མས་གདམས་པའི (other recension སྔར་གོམས་པའི).
- 101.4 བཟང་པོ་ཉམས་ཀྱང (other recension ཡིན་ཀྱང).
- 102.2 ང, the first glyph against the frame, which completes 102.1's བཀ as བཀང.
- 102.3 བེ in བེ་ཏ་ལི.
- 102.4 གསྨ (other recension ཀསྨ).
- 102.5 ཉམས and ཆུ in …དཀྲུགས་ཅིང་ཉམས་པའི་ཆུ་ལ་གྲིས་ཞལ་དུ་གསོལ་བ…. The other recension has only དཀྲུག་ཅིང་ཞལ་དུ་གསོལ་བ. The phrase is obscure; the drafter should mark the sense as uncertain.
- 102.5 ཙཎྜ.
- 103.1 བཀལ in ཕྲག་པ་བཀལ་ཏེ.
- 104.4 ན in མཐིང་ན (other recension ནག).
- 105.3 བཀང (fused with ནས; written with a tsheg, as usual).

## Fixes (11)
- Eight are tshegs missing where lines join: 98.5/99.1 (across the ornament), 99.2/3, 100.4/5, 101.5/102.1, 103.2/3 (འོང|ངོ), 105.2/3, 105.4/5 (དྲིལ|བུ) and 106.2/3.
- One fix covers a mid-line tsheg and a line join together: 104.3/4 གཡོན་དུབྷནྡྷ|ཐོགས → གཡོན་དུ་བྷནྡྷ་ཐོགས.
- One contraction is written out: 105.1 ཤར་འོངོ → ཤར་འོང་ངོ.
- **One misprint is corrected (rule 5b):** 106.1 དང་ཕྱུག་མ → དབང་ཕྱུག་མ. There is no བ even at ×10, and only "Īśvarī" makes sense. The note must give the print's reading.

## Kept, note only
- 99.1 བོད་ལ in the fixed formula ཚེ་འདས་ཀྱི་མིང་ནས་བོས་ལ་འདི་སྐད་དོ. The print has བོས at 101.5. The ད is clear. བོད could be an unprefixed spelling of 'bod "call", so the reading is not certain enough for a fix.
- 99.3 ལྗང་ནག་ཇམས་པ, where the sense wants "fierce" (རྔམ(ས)་པ). The letter is clearly ཇ.
- 101.1 རིག[?]་པ for རགས་པ (see above).
- 102.2 ཕྲ་མོ་དམར་མོ, where one expects a goddess's name (Pramohā?). Moderate.
- 103.3 སེང་ཧ་སྨུག, without མུ་ཁ.
- 104.1 རོ་ཁ་ཁྱེ (other recension ཁར་ཁྱེར).
- 104.3 ཀ་ཀ་མུ་ཁ. The print writes མུ་ཁ for མུ་ཀ throughout; that is its own spelling.
- 106.2 འགག་ལ་ཐུགས་པའི (for ཐུག).
- ཀྱཻ is printed with two e-signs every time, as in kha.
- དངངས is the print's spelling throughout.

## Where the print differs in sense from the other recension (the print is followed)
- 98.3–4: ངོ་མ་ཤེས་ཏེ་མ་འཕྲོད་པ་ཡོད་པས and འཇིགས་སྐྲག་ཆེ་རུ་འོངས་པས.
- 98.4: the print has ཕྲ་མེན་དང༔ སྨེ་མ་དང as two items, as at 98.4–5 in 010.
- 99.1: the print lacks "listen without distraction".
- 99.4: the print has ཡབ་ཀྱི་མགུལ, the father's neck.
- 100.2: Amoghasiddhi without ཡབ་ཡུམ, and མོས་པ་དང་གུས་པ without དུང་དུང.
- 100.4 and 101.3: sentences close with གྲོལ་ལོ༔ where the other recension runs on.
- 101.2: "the clear light the lama instructed before" and the mother and child clear lights "meet" (འཕྲད). The other recension has "the clear light one has habituated to" and "mingle".
- 102.1: the print lacks the announcement of the eight Gaurīs (…ཀོ་རཱི་མ་མོ་བརྒྱད་ཐོན་ནས…).
- 102.5–103.1: Caṇḍālī "loads head and body on her shoulder" instead of tearing them apart.
- 103.3: the print lacks "listen without distraction".
- 103.5–104.1: Śṛgālamukhā has no colour, and her razor and intestines are in the other hands.
- 104.4–5: Ulūkamukhā holds a sword in her left hand and eats flesh, instead of drinking blood from a conch.
- 105.3: the eastern gatekeeper is tiger-faced (སྟག་གདོང), not horse-faced, and holds a blood-filled skull-cup.
- 106.4: the first eastern yoginī holds a skull (ཐོད་པ), not a vajra; ཚངས་མ holds a lotus, not a wheel; ལྷ་ཆེན is white-green, not dark green.
